\subsection{One retained word through the whole congruence system}

\begin{statement}{E.55}{Proved}{The full preceding boundary family through every modulus prime to six}
Retain the actual source maps of E.51--E.53, with
$R=\prod_{p\geq5}\mathbf Z_p$.
Let $G_{\mathrm{old},\infty}$ be the actual closed joint
image of $\widehat B$ in the entire E.51 family: its
fixed $D_{23}$ and $G_L$ factors, its level-five and
level-seven symplectic factors, the full two-adic
class-two and three-adic class-three boundary factors,
and every full relative pro-$p$ boundary factor for
$p\geq5$. The Hurwitz source is retained through its
specified quotient map from $G_L$.
Write
$\rho_{\mathrm{old},\infty}:\widehat B\twoheadrightarrow
G_{\mathrm{old},\infty}$ for this continuous map.

Every one of the $432$ multiplier-one points, together
with every prescribed compatible full E.41 fibre and
full E.47 correction-image fibre, has a single
$f\in\widehat F'$ retaining all those images and
satisfying
\[
 \rho_R(f)=\rho_R(f_\sigma),\qquad
 \rho_L(f)=\rho_L(f_\sigma),\qquad
 \chi(\sigma)=1\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}
 \tag{E.55.1}
\]
for the same actual Galois element $\sigma$ selected
in E.43 and retained in E.51.
Thus all eight symplectic evaluations at every
modulus prime to six, and their full inverse limit,
are the evaluations of that same Galois word.
They satisfy the pentagon, the normalized cycle
relations, the specified periodic-braid conjugacies,
and the individual braid generation requirements.
The identity shadows on all full relative pro-$p$
boundary factors remain the prescribed identities.

Here are the exact joint source and word fibres.
For $m>1$ prime to six, put $g=\gcd(m,35)$ and define
$G_1=A_2$, $\rho_1=q_{A_2}$ and $C_1=1$.
For the other values of $g$, use the source $G_g$
of E.52. All maps below are the natural reductions
of those same source words. Put
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal Q_m&=A_{2m}\mathbin{\times_{A_{2g}}}G_g,\\
 K_m&=C_m\cap\ker(G_m\longrightarrow G_g).
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.55.2}
\]
For every finite old source $G_{\mathrm{old}}$ retaining
$P_{4m}=B/(\gamma_3(H)H^{4m})$, the maximum common
quotient through the specified maps is precisely
$\mathcal Q_m$, and the actual joint source is
\[
       G_{\mathrm{old}}\mathbin{\times_{\mathcal Q_m}}G_m.
 \tag{E.55.3}
\]
The corrected source supplied by $f$ is onto this
whole group. Such old sources are cofinal in the
stated E.51 family for each $m$.

Put $\mathcal A_R=\varprojlim_{(m,6)=1}A_{2m}$,
using divisibility transition maps, and put
\[
 \mathcal Q_R=\mathcal A_R\mathbin{\times_{A_{70}}}G_{35}.
 \tag{E.55.4}
\]
The full actual joint image, and the corrected image,
are both the profinite group
\[
       G_{\mathrm{old},\infty}
                   \mathbin{\times_{\mathcal Q_R}}G_R.
 \tag{E.55.5}
\]
Its new kernel over the old source is the exact
$\mathcal K_R^{35}$ of E.53.5.
All projections in these displays are continuous
epimorphisms induced by the displayed original
source maps.

For the chosen old word $f_0$ of E.51, define the
closed source subgroup
\[
 \mathscr K=R_{\mathrm{nil}}\cap\ker\rho_L
       \cap\ker\rho_5\cap\ker\rho_7
       \cap\ker\rho_{D_{23}}.
 \tag{E.55.6}
\]
The corrections $k\in\mathscr K$ in $f=f_0k$ form
the complete nonempty fibre
\[
 k_0\ker(\rho_R|_{\mathscr K}),\qquad
 \rho_R(k_0)=\rho_R(f_0)^{-1}\rho_R(f_\sigma).
 \tag{E.55.7}
\]
For the fixed full old value and fixed new Galois
value, all profinite commutator words are exactly
\[
 f\,\ker\bigl((\rho_{\mathrm{old},\infty},\rho_R)
                                          |_{\widehat F'}\bigr).
 \tag{E.55.8}
\]
These formulae retain every old parameter; a new
word is not selected separately for different
congruence moduli.
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We first identify each quotient map, then construct
one correction in the closed source subgroup, and
finally prove generation of the actual joint source.

\paragraph{Reduction and the whole common quotient.}
For $n\mid m$ with $m$ prime to six, reducing all
matrices in E.52's $48$ coordinates gives the actual
epimorphism $G_m\to G_n$. Its restriction
$C_m\to C_n$ is onto: in the coordinates
$C_m=\Phi_m(\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/m),V_3(\mathbf Z/m))$,
both factors reduce surjectively.
For the matrix factor this follows by lifting the
upper and lower elementary generators, which generate
over each local factor. The additive reduction is
the ordinary coordinate reduction in the proved
free rank-three summand. The reduction to $G_1=A_2$
is the parity quotient already specified in E.52.

In particular the two level maps give an actual
isomorphism
\[
                  G_{35}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_5\times_{A_2}G_7.
 \tag{E.55.9}
\]
It is injective by CRT on each of the $48$ matrix
coordinates and on the same outer coset action.
Its image has the full kernel over $A_2$, since
E.52 identifies that kernel with
$\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z/35)\times(\mathbf Z/35)^5$.
CRT identifies this kernel with the product of
the two stated level kernels. The outer $A_2$
map is onto, proving surjectivity in
\textup{(E.55.9)} as well.
This proves that the old level-five and level-seven
maps supply the indicated $G_{35}$ map with its
original source values.

The map
\[
 G_m\longrightarrow\mathcal Q_m,
       \qquad v\longmapsto(\operatorname{ab}_{2m}(v),v\bmod g)
 \tag{E.55.10}
\]
is onto and has kernel $K_m$.
The kernel assertion is its definition, using
$\ker(G_m\to A_{2m})=C_m$ from E.52.
For surjectivity, take a pair $(a,h)$ in the
displayed fibre product and lift $a$ to $v\in G_m$.
The element $h(v\bmod g)^{-1}$ lies in $C_g$.
Lift it through the just-proved epimorphism
$C_m\to C_g$ and multiply that lift by $v$.
Its image under \textup{(E.55.10)} is $(a,h)$.
This proves the assertion through explicit
quotient maps, including the case $g=1$.

The old sources contain the required abelian
quotient. Indeed
\[
 \gamma_3(H)\subset F',\qquad H^{4m}\subset F^{2m}
 \tag{E.55.11}
\]
give an actual epimorphism $P_{4m}\to A_{2m}$.
To see that $P_{4m}$ belongs to the specified old
boundary system, the class-two Hall coordinates
of its geometric kernel are modulo $4m$ in degree
one and modulo
$\gcd(4m,\binom{4m}{2})=2m$ in degree two.
These moduli follow directly from the power
formula and the commutator formula: powers of
the basis elements impose $4m$ on each coordinate,
and a power of a product of two basis elements
also imposes $\binom{4m}{2}$ on their commutator.
Conversely these moduli annihilate every $4m$-th
power in the collected class-two group.
The two natural maps therefore give the CRT
isomorphism
\[
                    P_{4m}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_4\times_{B/H}P_m.
 \tag{E.55.12}
\]
On $H$ its coordinate maps are precisely the CRT
maps from $(4m,2m)$ to $(4,2)$ and $(m,m)$.
The odd class-two exponent-$m$ group is the product
of its prime-power Sylow quotients. Each is a
finite characteristic quotient of the corresponding
full pro-$p$ boundary factor retained in E.42.
E.41 retains $P_4$. Thus these are actual old
quotients, and adjoining $P_{4m}$ only refines
within the specified system. Adjoining any finite
list of such quotients has the same property.

Consequently $G_{\mathrm{old}}$ has the map to
$\mathcal Q_m$ supplied by its $A_{2m}$ map and
its $G_g$ map from \textup{(E.55.9)}.
The compatibility over $A_{2g}$ holds on $s,r$,
since all maps are evaluations of the same original
source. Its image is the whole $\mathcal Q_m$,
because the source composite agrees with the
surjection \textup{(E.55.10)}.

By E.53, the exact image of the closed subgroup
\textup{(E.55.6)} is
\[
                         \rho_R(\mathscr K)=\mathcal K_R^{35}.
 \tag{E.55.13}
\]
Every remaining old boundary factor kills
$R_{\mathrm{nil}}$: its restriction to $H$ is
nilpotent at each finite level. The full relative
pro-$p$ factors have finite $p$-group quotients,
each of finite nilpotency class, and hence kill
$R_{\mathrm{nil}}$ in their inverse limits too.
The separate $D_{23}$ kernel in
\textup{(E.55.6)} retains the complete old fixed
finite source. Thus
\[
              \mathscr K\subset\ker\rho_{\mathrm{old},\infty}.
 \tag{E.55.14}
\]

Reduction of E.53.5 modulo $m$ is exactly $K_m$:
at five and seven it gives the first matrix
congruence subgroup and the corresponding additive
multiple; at every other prime it gives the
entire matrix and additive factors of $C_m$.
This is exactly the kernel of reduction from
$C_m$ to $C_g$ in E.52's coordinates.
Equations \textup{(E.55.13)--(E.55.14)} therefore give
$K_m\subset\rho_m(\ker\rho_{\mathrm{old}})$.
The common map to $\mathcal Q_m$ gives the reverse
inclusion. We have proved the exact equality
\[
                     \rho_m(\ker\rho_{\mathrm{old}})=K_m.
 \tag{E.55.15}
\]
The actual joint source is subdirect. Its kernel
over the old projection is $K_m$, and its quotient
comparison is \textup{(E.55.10)}. Lifting an old
element and then multiplying by this pure kernel
gives every compatible pair, proving
\textup{(E.55.3)} and the asserted maximum common
quotient.

For the inverse limit, the old maps
$P_{4m}\to A_{2m}$ give the continuous onto map
$G_{\mathrm{old},\infty}\to\mathcal A_R$.
Surjectivity follows either from the same source
values or from nonempty closed finite fibres.
Together with \textup{(E.55.9)} it gives the actual
map to \textup{(E.55.4)}. The kernel of
$G_R\to\mathcal Q_R$ is
$C_R\cap\ker(G_R\to G_{35})=\mathcal K_R^{35}$.
The surjectivity argument for
\textup{(E.55.10)} applies using the onto map
$C_R\to C_{35}$ and the compact lift of each
$\mathcal A_R$ value.
The same kernel equality as
\textup{(E.55.15)}, using
\textup{(E.55.13)--(E.55.14)}, now proves the
actual source identity \textup{(E.55.5)}.

\paragraph{A single correction retaining every old parameter.}
Take the complete E.51 word $f_0$ for the prescribed
old point and full boundary parameters. Retain its
same actual $\sigma$ from E.43.11.
The equality $\chi(\sigma)=1$ there is in all of
$\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}$; it therefore holds
at every new congruence level simultaneously.
Both $f_0$ and $f_\sigma$ belong to $\widehat F'$,
so
\[
       d=\rho_R(f_0)^{-1}\rho_R(f_\sigma)\in C_R.
 \tag{E.55.16}
\]
E.51 supplies their equality under both $\rho_5$
and $\rho_7$. Under E.52's actual reduction maps,
the element $d$ therefore lies in
$C_R\cap\ker\rho_5\cap\ker\rho_7
=\mathcal K_R^{35}$.
Lift $d$ by the continuous surjection
\textup{(E.55.13)} and set $f=f_0k$.
The subgroup $\mathscr K$ lies in $\widehat F'$
and in the full old source kernel by
\textup{(E.55.14)}. The word $f$ consequently
retains every old value and has the required
new value \textup{(E.55.1)}.
This constructs one element of the closed full
source, with every prime and precision already
included in its target.

All $48$ induced evaluations of $f$ agree with
those of $f_\sigma$. The five-strand pentagon
and the three normalized evaluations are thus
literally the corresponding Galois evaluations.
The multiplier is exactly one, including on
each transvection and each periodic braid.
The resulting map on each new braid target is
the specified quotient map precomposed with
the actual Galois braid automorphism used in
E.38 and E.50. It is onto that target and has
the stated full-twist and periodic conjugacy
identities. The same assertion holds for their
actual joint inverse-limit image: all its
components are precomposed with that one
automorphism. It also holds after adjoining
the Hurwitz component, whose source values
factor through the retained $G_L$ map.

\paragraph{Generation of the whole common source after correction.}
For a specified finite target $G$ write
$\rho_G^f:\widehat B\to G$ for the normalized
source map with generator values
$s\mapsto\rho_G(s)\rho_G(f)$ and
$r\mapsto\rho_G(f)^{-1}\rho_G(r)$.
The order relations for these values hold in
every old factor by E.51 and in every new
factor by \textup{(E.55.1)}.
They therefore give actual continuous
homomorphisms from $\widehat B$ to their
common source targets.

On $G_L,G_5,G_7,G_R$ these are the original
maps precomposed with the same normalized
Galois automorphism $\alpha_\sigma$ of
$\widehat B$. This automorphism preserves
$\widehat F$, its characteristic subgroup
$\widehat H$, and $R_{\mathrm{nil}}$.
Transporting E.53.5 by $\alpha_\sigma$ gives
\[
 \rho_R^f\bigl(R_{\mathrm{nil}}\cap\ker\rho_L^f
                \cap\ker\rho_5^f\cap\ker\rho_7^f\bigr)
                         =\mathcal K_R^{35}.
 \tag{E.55.17}
\]
For the moment the separate $D_{23}$ condition
has not been imposed in this display.

Every finite solvable quotient of
$\mathcal K_R^{35}$ has order prime to six.
Its unrestricted $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_p)$
factors are topologically perfect. Its remaining
matrix factors are pro-five and pro-seven, and
its additive factors have primes at least five.
This proves the assertion also for each finite
reduction $K_m$.
The image of the subgroup in
\textup{(E.55.17)} under $\rho_{D_{23}}^f$ is a
solvable group with primes only two and three.
Its actual subdirect image with $K_m$ has
trivial common quotient: a common quotient
would be solvable and its order would have
both of these disjoint sets of prime divisors.
The projection kernels therefore give the
whole direct product. Imposing
$\ker\rho_{D_{23}}^f$ preserves the full
image $K_m$.

All remaining corrected old boundary maps
still kill $R_{\mathrm{nil}}$.
For each finite factor this follows by
applying its nilpotency class to the image
of the lower central series of $\widehat H$.
Their $H$ images are in the indicated
geometric kernels because $f\in\widehat H$
and the induced map on $B/H$ is the
identity. Thus the corrected joint image
contains the entire pure $K_m$ over
$G_{\mathrm{old}}$.

The corrected projection onto
$G_{\mathrm{old}}$ is onto by E.51.
The two corrected maps to $\mathcal Q_m$
agree. On $A_{2m}$ they are the original
map, since $f\in\widehat F'$ has trivial
image there. On $G_g$ they are the same
Galois precomposition, by the level-five
and level-seven equalities and
\textup{(E.55.9)}. These are exactly the
two components of \textup{(E.55.2)}.
The corrected image therefore lies in
\textup{(E.55.3)}, projects onto its old
factor, and contains its entire kernel
$K_m$ over that factor. Multiplying by
that kernel proves onto generation of
the whole fibre product.

This argument applies at every finite
old level and every $m$ after adjoining
the specified $P_{4m}$. Projection gives
the assertion before that refinement.
Any finite collection of levels is
dominated by one such old level and by
their least common multiple $m$.
The corrected closed image is therefore
onto every finite projection of
\textup{(E.55.5)}, and compactness makes
it the entire displayed profinite group.
Its restriction to $\widehat H$ is onto
the actual geometric kernel as well:
the retained $B/H$ map is the identity,
so a preimage of that kernel already
lies in $\widehat H$.

Finally, multiplying two preimages
under $\rho_R|_{\mathscr K}$ gives
exactly \textup{(E.55.7)}. Multiplying
two words in $\widehat F'$ with the
same full old and new values gives
exactly \textup{(E.55.8)}.
Every relation and generation assertion
above depends on those specified values,
so all words in this full fibre satisfy
them. This completes the exact source,
parameter and inverse-limit comparisons.
\end{proof}
E.56_audited_source:
\subsection{The full integral symplectic targets and their retained products}

\begin{statement}{E.56}{Proved}{Exact transvection targets at every modulus prime to six}
Let $J$ be the alternating chain matrix of E.52.7, put
$\Omega=J^{-1}$, and write
\[
 a=e_1,\qquad b=e_2,\qquad c=e_1+e_3,\qquad d=e_4,
 \qquad W=\langle a,b\rangle.
 \tag{E.56.1}
\]
For $T=\mathbf Z/m$, where $(m,6)=1$, or
$T=R=\prod_{p\ge5}\mathbf Z_p$, define
\[
 \begin{split}
 T_v(t)&=I+t vv^{\mathsf t}J,\\
 \mathcal P(T)&=\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{Sp}_4(T,J)}(c),\\
 \mathcal P^{\rm rt}(T)&=J\mathcal P(T)J^{-1}
                  \subset\operatorname{Sp}_4(T,\Omega).
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.56.2}
\]
The four original column transvections
$T_a(1),T_b(1),T_{c-a}(1),T_d(1)$ generate
$\operatorname{Sp}_4(T,J)$; the first three generate
exactly $\mathcal P(T)$. For $T=R$, generation means
closed topological generation. The exact structure of
the latter group is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathcal P(T)=U(T)\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_2(T),\\
 U(T)=\{n(w,z):w\in W(T),\ z\in T\},\\
 n(w,z)=I+w c^{\mathsf t}J+c w^{\mathsf t}J
                         +z c c^{\mathsf t}J,\\
 n(w,z)n(w',z')
     =n(w+w',z+z'+\langle w,w'\rangle).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{E.56.3}
\]
Here $\langle u,v\rangle=u^{\mathsf t}Jv$, and the
displayed $\operatorname{SL}_2$ acts on $W$ and fixes
$c,d$ individually.

In the literal right convention of E.52, the generators
are $M_i=T_{e_i}(1)^{\mathsf t}$. Their full image is
$\operatorname{Sp}_4(T,\Omega)$ and their first-three
image is exactly $\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(T)$. Those first
three matrices fix the row $c^{\mathsf t}$, or equivalently the column
$Jc=-e_4$. The precise source comparison is
\[
 J^{-1}M_iJ=T_{e_i}(-1),\qquad
 \operatorname{Ad}(J^{-1})\circ q^{\rm rt}_{T,n}
       =q^{\rm col}_{T,n}\circ\iota,
 \quad \iota(\sigma_i)=\sigma_i^{-1},\quad n=4,5.
 \tag{E.56.4}
\]
The map $\iota$ is the actual involutive braid
automorphism given on all the displayed generators.

Retain the literal Ferrari maps to $T_L,T_{23}$ and
the exact quotient $S_L$ from E.38--E.43, and the
four- and five-strand Hurwitz maps to $A_{96}$ from
E.46. With their specified original generator maps,
the actual four-strand joint image is
\[
 \bigl(T_{23}\times_{S_L}T_L\bigr)
                 \times\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(T)\times A_{96},
 \tag{E.56.5}
\]
and the actual five-strand joint image is
\[
                  \operatorname{Sp}_4(T,\Omega)\times A_{96}.
 \tag{E.56.6}
\]
In particular the actual joint image of the two
four-strand maps to $T_L$ and the new symplectic
target is $T_L\times\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(T)$.
All these statements retain their reductions and
the actual inverse-limit maps. The corrected words
of E.55 generate the same displayed joint targets.
\end{statement}

\begin{proof}
We give elementary matrix elimination and then determine
the common quotients through the specified braid maps.

\paragraph{The exact conventions and the Heisenberg subgroup.}
The integral matrix with columns $a,b,c,d$ has determinant
one and satisfies
\[
 (a\ b\ c\ d)^{\mathsf t}J(a\ b\ c\ d)
       =\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}
                       \oplus
        \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{E.56.7}
\]
Thus $W$ and $\langle c,d\rangle$ are orthogonal
symplectic planes. Direct multiplication gives
$T_v(t)T_v(u)=T_v(t+u)$ and
$gT_v(t)g^{-1}=T_{gv}(t)$ for a symplectic $g$.
The first two transvections give the upper and lower
elementary matrices on $W$. For a unit $u$, put
\[
 w_W(u)=T_a(u)T_b(u^{-1})T_a(u).
 \tag{E.56.8}
\]
Its matrix on $W$ is
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&u\\-u^{-1}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
and $w_W(u)w_W(-1)=\operatorname{diag}(u,u^{-1})$.

The half turn $h=w_W(1)^2$ sends $c-a$ to $c+a$
and fixes $c,d$. Orthogonality of $a,c$ gives the
exact polynomial identities
\[
 \begin{split}
 T_{c+a}(t)T_{c-a}(t)&=T_c(2t)T_a(2t),\\
 T_{c+a}(t)T_a(-t)T_c(-t)
      &=I+t\bigl(a c^{\mathsf t}J+c a^{\mathsf t}J\bigr).
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.56.9}
\]
Consequently the first three original transvections
give $T_c(t)$ and $n(ta,0)$ for every parameter $t$.
Conjugation by $w_W(1)$ gives $n(tb,0)$ as well.
For finite $T$, every parameter is an integer power
of the corresponding unit-parameter transvection;
division by two in the first formula is legitimate
because two is a unit. Formula E.56.3 follows by
multiplication, and in particular
\[
 \begin{split}
 n(xa+yb,z)&=n(xa,0)n(yb,0)T_c(z-xy),\\
 [n(xa,0),n(yb,0)]&=T_c(2xy).
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.56.10}
\]
These are actual words in the original three
generators, with every parameter and central term
retained.

To identify the whole stabilizer, a symplectic matrix
fixing $c$ induces a determinant-one matrix $A$ on
$c^\perp/Tc\simeq W$. Multiplying by the inverse
of the displayed lift of $A$ makes that induced
action the identity. The resulting matrix sends
\[
 c\longmapsto c,\qquad
 d\longmapsto d+w+zc,\qquad
 v\longmapsto v+\langle w,v\rangle c\quad(v\in W).
 \tag{E.56.11}
\]
The last formula is forced by pairing its image
with the image of $d$. Hence it is precisely
$n(w,z)$, uniquely. This proves E.56.3 through
the indicated matrix map.

Over a local ring $\mathbf Z/p^r$, every
$A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\\gamma&\delta\end{smallmatrix}\right)$
of determinant one has a unit in its first column.
When $\alpha$ is a unit, the exact factorization is
\[
 A=E_{21}(\gamma/\alpha)
          \operatorname{diag}(\alpha,\alpha^{-1})
                                      E_{12}(\beta/\alpha).
 \tag{E.56.12}
\]
Otherwise left multiplication by $w_W(1)$ makes
the top entry of that column a unit. This proves
elementary generation of the required
$\operatorname{SL}_2$ and, with E.56.10, proves
that the first three original generators give
the full stabilizer over each local ring.

\paragraph{Eliminating a primitive vector.}
Adding $T_d(1)$ gives the same elementary
$\operatorname{SL}_2$ on $\langle c,d\rangle$.
We describe an actual word taking any primitive
vector
$v=v_W+zc+td$ to $c$ over $\mathbf Z/p^r$.
If neither $z$ nor $t$ is a unit, a coordinate
of $v_W$ is a unit. Choose $w=a$ or $b$ so that
$\langle w,v_W\rangle$ is a unit. Multiplication
by $n(w,0)$ changes the $c$-coordinate to
$z+\langle w,v_W\rangle$, which is then a unit.
If the $d$-coordinate is not yet a unit, the
plane rotation $w_{\langle c,d\rangle}(1)$
makes it one. Rename the resulting coordinates
$v_W,z,t$, with $t$ a unit.

Now apply, in this order,
\[
 n(-t^{-1}v_W,0),\quad T_c(-z/t),\quad
 \operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})\big|_{\langle c,d\rangle},\quad
 w_{\langle c,d\rangle}(1).
 \tag{E.56.13}
\]
The first map removes $v_W$ and leaves $z$ unchanged,
because $\langle -t^{-1}v_W,v_W\rangle=0$.
The next removes $z$; the last two send $td$ to
$d$ and then to $c$. Every factor has already been
expressed as a word in the four original transvections.

For an arbitrary symplectic $g$, apply this word
to $gc$. The resulting product fixes $c$, so it
belongs to the explicitly generated stabilizer.
This proves generation of the entire symplectic
group over each local ring. For a general $m$,
CRT parameters supported at a single prime-power
factor make each original transvection the identity
in all other factors. The local words therefore
give the whole product over $\mathbf Z/m$.
The stabilizer proof has the same property.
Compactness and the cofinal divisibility system
of moduli give the asserted closed images over $R$.

The transpose convention is also literal.
Since $J^{\mathsf t}=-J$, multiplication gives
$T_{e_i}(1)^{\mathsf t}=JT_{e_i}(-1)J^{-1}$.
The inverse-generator substitution preserves both
the Artin braid relations and the distant commutation
relations, and its square is the identity.
It is therefore the automorphism $\iota$ in E.56.4.
The equalities on every braid generator prove that
displayed morphism. They also prove both stated
fixed-vector descriptions, including $Jc=-e_4$.
The saved level-five and level-seven permutation
maps are compared with these transposes on every
nonzero vector in the certificate below.

\paragraph{Perfectness and the actual simple quotients.}
The groups just generated are perfect at every
finite level. On a symplectic plane, conjugation
by $\operatorname{diag}(2,1/2)$ multiplies the
upper elementary parameter by four; its commutator
with $E_{12}(t)$ is $E_{12}(3t)$.
The lower parameter is multiplied by $1/4$, and
the corresponding difference $-3/4$ is a unit.
Thus the plane $\operatorname{SL}_2$ is perfect.
Its commutators with $n(ta,0)$ give all those
elements, since the difference on $a$ is one.
Its difference on $b$ is $-1/2$, also a unit,
so the same holds for $n(tb,0)$.
Their commutators in E.56.10 give the whole
central subgroup. Hence $\mathcal P(T)$ is perfect.
For the full symplectic group, the primitive-vector
elimination conjugates each original transvection
to one in a symplectic plane; every generator is
therefore a commutator. This proves perfectness
of the full group too.

We include the finite-field simplicity argument
needed at arbitrary primes. The projective action
of $\operatorname{Sp}_4(\mathbf F_p,J)$ on lines
has kernel exactly $\{\pm I\}$: a linear operator
fixing all lines is scalar, and preservation of
the alternating form gives these two scalars.
The stabilizer of the line $\mathbf F_pc$ has
the three orbits of sizes
\[
                    1,\qquad p^2+p,\qquad p^3.
 \tag{E.56.14}
\]
For the perpendicular lines different from $c$,
the plane $\operatorname{SL}_2$ is transitive on
the nonzero $W$ component and $n(w,0)$ changes
the $c$ component arbitrarily. For a line not
perpendicular to $c$, scale its $d$ coordinate
to one; $n(w,z)$ then moves it to $d$.
This proves the orbit assertion using the actual
stabilizer already constructed.

A block containing the line of $c$ is a union
of these stabilizer orbits. The two intermediate
possible sizes are $p^2+p+1$ and $p^3+1$.
Neither divides the total number
$N=p^3+p^2+p+1$: one has
$N=p(p^2+p+1)+1$, and $p^3+1$ lies strictly
between $N/2$ and $N$. The faithful projective
action is consequently primitive.
The subgroup $\{T_c(t):t\in\mathbf F_p\}$ is
abelian and normal in the line stabilizer, since
replacing $c$ by $uc$ replaces $t$ by $u^2t$.
Its conjugates generate the group by the proved
transvection generation.

For completeness, the elementary normal-subgroup
argument now proves simplicity. A nontrivial normal
subgroup of a faithful primitive permutation group
is transitive. Modulo such a subgroup, every
conjugate of the displayed abelian subgroup has
the same image: write each group element as a
normal-subgroup element times an element of the
point stabilizer, which normalizes that subgroup.
The quotient is therefore generated by one
abelian image. Perfectness makes it trivial.
We have proved simplicity of
$\operatorname{PSp}_4(\mathbf F_p)$ for every
$p\ge5$. Simplicity of
$\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ is proved
by the same normal-subgroup argument in E.53.

The kernel of reduction from a matrix group
modulo $p^r$ to its reduction modulo $p$ is
a $p$-group: successive kernels embed, by
$1+p^jA\mapsto A$, into additive matrix spaces
over $\mathbf F_p$.
The structure E.56.3 therefore shows that
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathcal P(\mathbf Z/p^r)&\longrightarrow
                         \operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p),\\
 \operatorname{Sp}_4(\mathbf Z/p^r)&\longrightarrow
                         \operatorname{PSp}_4(\mathbf F_p)
 \end{split}
 \tag{E.56.15}
\]
have solvable kernels. These are the actual
maps induced on $c^\perp/Tc$, followed by
reduction and the scalar quotient, in the first
case, and the actual reduction and scalar
quotient in the second.

Every proper normal subgroup of either source
in E.56.15 is contained in the stated kernel.
Indeed its image in the simple target is
trivial or the whole target. In the latter
case the resulting quotient is an image of
the solvable kernel; it is also a quotient of
a perfect group and hence must be trivial.
Thus every nontrivial quotient retains the
specified simple quotient in E.56.15.
This proves the required assertion including
all central and higher congruence kernels.

\paragraph{The complete target product with $T_L$.}
Consider the actual subdirect image of the two
four-strand maps to $T_L$ and
$\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(\mathbf Z/m)$.
A nontrivial Goursat common quotient is perfect,
because the latter group is perfect. It has a
nonabelian simple quotient. The matrix target
is the product of its prime-power factors;
their images in a simple group commute and
are normal, so exactly one factor supplies
that simple quotient. E.56.15 identifies it
with the specified
$\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ map, up
to an automorphism of that target.

For $p=5,7$, this would force that actual
projective matrix map to factor through
$T_L$. The complete literal products
$T_L\times\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(\mathbf F_p)$
proved in E.50 and E.51 exclude that factorization.
For $p\ge11$, the order of
$\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ has a
factor $p$, whereas the retained exact order
of $T_L$ has prime divisors only $2,3,5,7$.
This excludes every possible common quotient.
Goursat therefore gives the whole actual
product $T_L\times\mathcal P^{\rm rt}(\mathbf Z/m)$.

The projection
$T_{23}\times_{S_L}T_L\to T_L$ has solvable
kernel. In a common quotient with the perfect
matrix target, quotienting by the image of
that kernel gives a common quotient with
$T_L$, just excluded. The original common
quotient would then be solvable and perfect,
and hence trivial. This proves the product
with the whole old four-strand target.

\paragraph{The alternating factor and the full inverse limit.}
The simple group $A_{96}$ is neither
$\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_p)$ nor
$\operatorname{PSp}_4(\mathbf F_p)$ for any
$p\ge5$. The matrix group orders are
\[
 \frac{p(p^2-1)}2,\qquad
                 \frac{p^4(p^2-1)(p^4-1)}2.
 \tag{E.56.16}
\]
For the second formula, count a symplectic
basis: its successive choices number
$(p^4-1),p^3,(p^2-1),p$, and then divide by
the two scalar matrices. The first formula
is the same basis count in dimension two.
Equality with $96!/2$ would imply $p\le96$,
since $p$ divides that order. Both displayed
orders would then be smaller than $96^{10}/2$,
while $96!\ge77^{20}>96^{10}$.
This proves the asserted exclusions.

It follows from E.56.15 that no finite matrix
target in the statement has an $A_{96}$
quotient. A simple quotient of a product
comes from one of its factors, as above.
The old target has no such quotient either:
its solvable kernel is killed in a simple
nonabelian quotient, and the order of $T_L$
has no factor eleven. The actual four- and
five-strand Hurwitz maps are onto $A_{96}$
by E.46. Goursat now proves exactly
E.56.5 and E.56.6 at every finite modulus.

Every finite collection of congruence levels
is dominated by their least common multiple.
The closed actual images over $R$ therefore
surject onto every finite projection of the
displayed products. Compactness proves the
same product identities over $R$.

Finally E.55 retains the same Galois word in
all matrix and $T_L$ components and in the
Hurwitz component. Their corrected maps
are the displayed original joint maps
precomposed with one actual braid
automorphism, so their images are the same
products. The separate corrected $T_{23}$
map is onto and agrees in $S_L$ by E.55.
The maximum solvable quotient of $T_L$ is
the specified $S_L$; the new matrix and
alternating factors are perfect. Thus the
same solvable-kernel Goursat argument gives
the whole corrected product E.56.5.
All inverse-limit comparisons retain these
same maps. This proves the final assertion.
\end{proof}
